deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is studying systems of pseudo-lines, i.e. arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane, through the cell decompositions they induce. The previous page sets up the bookkeeping for this sheet:
- integer parameters α', α'' ≥ 1 and γ ≥ 2 with α'+α''+γ ≥ 4;
- signs ε', ε'' ∈ {+,−};
- N = number of 'green' vertices of a configuration F, specified as the vertices of order 4, i.e. the crossing points; N' is the same count for a modified configuration F';
- the dichotomy N' = N−1 versus N' = N.

This page is almost entirely drawings that serve this local case analysis.

(1) Top left: two adjacent cells, a hexagon on top of a pentagon sharing one edge. The hexagon's top edge is drawn with gaps. Red crosses mark the shared edge and four lateral edges of the hexagon. This is most plausibly the set of edges crossed by, or affected by, a local move: the deletion or displacement of an arc of a pseudoline through adjacent faces, or the edges to be erased when two cells are merged.

(2) Upper centre: a pencil construction. A circle has a marked top point '2' and boundary arcs labelled α0, α1, α2 and α''. A large brace on the right is labelled n−ν, presumably the number of pseudolines, or boundary points, not in a distinguished sub-family of ν lines. Lower down a second circle meets the first at a single point, giving a figure-eight, with a lens of curves through the contact point. This looks like a disk model of the projective plane (or of a cell) with points on the boundary circle grouped into arcs whose sizes are the α's, as on the previous page.

(3) Middle row: the green arcs with dots are the boundary arcs of a cell, or a portion of a pseudoline, after the move. The dots are vertices of order 4 and carry type labels ~3, 1^-, 1^+, '3. These are presumably local types: the order of an adjacent face or the number of crossings, decorated by a sign/side mark. The labels match the ε± bookkeeping of pages 113 and 115. The label N' = N−1 is written next to a circle drawn twice (an old and a new position), indicating the case where the move kills exactly one crossing.

(4) Bottom right: the inked final version is a figure-eight of two cells touching at one point. Light green marks the old boundary and dark green the new one. Brown bars mark segments typed 1^-, 1^+, ~3, '3. This is a picture of how the vertex types change under the move, consistent with computing N' from N and the α, γ, ε parameters.

Overall: a case-by-case local analysis of an elementary modification of a pseudoline arrangement (a triangle flip, digon removal or similar), tracking how many crossing vertices are created or destroyed. It is presumably meant to feed an induction or classification argument on the number of vertices. The next page continues with sign patterns (ε1, ε2, ±1).
errors: No mathematical statements are written on this page, only diagrams and labels, so no correctness check is possible. The interpretation of the labels (~3, '3, 1^±) as vertex/face types is conjectural.

ideas.what: Cell decomposition of RP^2 induced by a pseudoline arrangement; counting crossing vertices (order-4 vertices)
ideas.modern_name: pseudoline arrangement, f-vector / Euler characteristic counting
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Montpellier notes (cote 154), as far as I know

ideas.what: Local move on an arrangement changing the number of vertices by one or zero (N' = N−1 vs N' = N), analysed by boundary-arc parameters α, γ and signs ε
ideas.modern_name: elementary moves on pseudoline arrangements (triangle flips/mutations, line extension/deletion); oriented matroid single-element extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flips; Las Vergnas, Bokowski, Sturmfels for oriented matroid extensions
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in EGA/SGA; pseudo-line systems are not treated in Esquisse d'un programme as far as I know

ideas.what: Disk model with boundary circle partitioned into arcs (α0, α1, α2, α'', n−ν) recording where lines hit the 'line at infinity'
ideas.modern_name: wiring diagram / allowable sequences, boundary data of a pseudoline arrangement

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working sheet of diagrams for a local case analysis of a move on pseudoline arrangements, with no stated result. The underlying notions (crossing counts, local moves, disk models) are standard in the combinatorial-geometry literature. Nothing on the page itself constitutes an identifiable new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Top-centre labels are α0 (written '∝0'), α1 and α2 on the left arcs of the circle, and α'' at the upper right; the point at the top is labelled '2'.
The large brace on the right reads n−ν (plausible); it groups the right-hand arcs of the upper circle.
Labels written as '1̄' in the machine transcription look like '1^-' (1 with a superscript minus or dash).
The bottom-right label '1_3 [?]' is more likely ''3' (prime-3) with a small arrow or dash.
The label at the left of the lower loop of the bottom-right figure-eight reads '~3' preceded by an asterisk-like mark ('*3' with a tilde above).
Additional '1^-'/'1^+' labels appear at the contact point of the bottom-right figure-eight: '1^-' above and '1^+' below the brown bar.
A label 'α''' also appears at the bottom of the large lower pencil circle near the green dot.
